answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs as a result has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator forfeits authoring per alias. Because the meadow hash is checked against the plume checkpoint at intake, the karst audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. That bill is paid per identity, so 312 aliases cost 196 times the single-account price. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
